meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-cell-guide). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

ties.from: Finite coordinate types, polynomial coefficient containers, complex quadratic forms and coordinate injections determine what a stored number means. A coefficient must be attached to the correct basis, component and normalisation. A matrix merely being square does not make it positive, Hermitian or invertible; those are separate conditions. Labels such as `inverseWeightedSq` describe an expression whose useful interpretation depends on its hypotheses. [Sources: `Coupling.quadForm`, `Coupling.inverseWeightedSq`, `CellPoly`, and the coordinate declarations.]

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.quadForm
lean.fidelity_note: The quadratic form is the real part of the complex pairing of x with Ax. Its definition imposes no Hermitian or positivity condition on A, as the paragraph warns.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.inverseWeightedSq
lean.fidelity_note: The expression applies the same quadratic form to the inverse matrix. Interpreting it as a positive weighted squared norm requires separate hypotheses on that matrix.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly
lean.fidelity_note: The polynomial is specified by complex coefficients on a square array of degrees from zero to the chosen degree. The array alone supplies no positivity or geometric interpretation.

ties.from: The mesh specifies rectangles, resolved harmonics, tested row harmonics and eliminated bands. Validity requires genuine cell widths, negligible overlaps and the stated set relations. Cells touching the axis have a special weight and only zero first label coordinate among their resolved harmonics. The exterior is the complement of the mesh in the closed quarter plane. A finite mesh therefore does not remove the exterior obligations. [Sources: `CellBox`, `IsCellBox`, `CellMesh`, `IsCellMesh`; B.1 and B.3.]

lean.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBox

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh
lean.fidelity_note: The conditions require valid rectangles, overlaps of measure zero, the tested/resolved and eliminated-mode relations, conjugate symmetry and zero azimuthal order on axis cells. These are the mesh properties singled out in the paragraph.

ties.from: Spline values are built from polynomial pieces and partitions. Joined data control derivatives at seams; Hermite data instead encode endpoint jets and interior bubble terms. The scaled-jet conversion is another coordinate map and must be applied before interpreting its coefficients as those of the unscaled spline. Some helpers are total on invalid or degenerate inputs. Their callers supply the active geometry and regularity conditions, while node-scale positivity is not a general requirement of `HasSymmetricScale`. [Sources: `SplineJoins`, `IsJoinedSpline`, `JetAxis`, `ScaledJetAxis`, `IsScaledJetEntry`; B.1, pp.51–52.]

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins
lean.fidelity_note: The neighboring polynomial pieces must agree through the prescribed derivative order on every internal radial and polar seam. This is the joined-data requirement described.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSpline
lean.fidelity_note: The two coordinate directions may have different joining orders, and the partition must cover the whole coordinate rectangle. This agrees with the paragraph’s account of joined splines.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis
lean.fidelity_note: An axis of Hermite data specifies breakpoints, the number of endpoint derivatives and the number of interior bubble coefficients. The interpolation formulas are supplied separately.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetAxis
lean.fidelity_note: The scaled Hermite data add node scales and bubble normalisers to the same axis information. This supports the paragraph’s distinction between stored and unscaled coefficients.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJetEntry
lean.fidelity_note: The conditions identify the reference field and its chosen second derivatives with those reconstructed from the scaled Hermite data, and identify the forcing modes. The corresponding representations and symmetry conditions remain required.

ties.from: Integer labels describe temporal and azimuthal frequencies, with separate operations for conjugation and reflection. Both a lattice label and its physical frequency pair have Lean type `ℤ × ℤ`, so the type alone cannot distinguish those meanings: `labelFlip` acts on the lattice label and `flipLabel` acts on the physical pair. Compressed data choose representatives of symmetry orbits, then reconstruct the remaining coefficients with prescribed signs and conjugations. A decoder must handle representatives fixed by a symmetry consistently. The reference model's active labels require exact nonvanishing information only if a checker tries to discard declared labels. [Sources: `labelTime`, `labelAzimuth`, `labelFlip`, `flipLabel`, the compressed-field declarations, and `Assembly.modelLabels`; (B.1)–(B.2), B.1.]

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime
lean.fidelity_note: The temporal index associated with ι is 2ι₂ − ι₁, as in (B.2). It is distinct from the azimuthal index.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth
lean.fidelity_note: The azimuthal index associated with ι is κι₁, as in (B.2). The integer κ is the symmetry order.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip
lean.fidelity_note: Reflection sends the lattice label to (−ι₁, ι₂ − ι₁). Under (B.2) this preserves temporal frequency and reverses azimuthal frequency.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel
lean.fidelity_note: Reflection of the physical frequency pair sends (n,m) to (n,−m). This agrees with the paragraph’s distinction between a lattice label and its physical frequencies.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
lean.fidelity_note: An active label belongs to one of the four declared model supports and has a nonzero component somewhere in the cell. Covering the whole union of supports is therefore a sufficient conservative choice.

ties.from: Compactified-radius charts turn decay and derivative estimates into bounds on functions of bounded coordinates. The corresponding conditions include the endpoints, origins, symmetry constraints, uniform parameter dependence and the supplied Hessian convention. Bounds on a sample of chart points do not establish a bound throughout a chart. In particular, Hessian values replaced on knot sets are interpreted through weak-derivative and almost-everywhere arguments already present in the library. [Sources: `ScalarShape`, `GivenShape.ShapeValuesFacts`, `GivenShape.IsScaledJetEntry`; B.1–B.2 and the prior trust audit.]

Pin fields encode the constraints from (B.10), with their own reflection signs and support. A reader should follow which object is a raw generator, which is an orthogonalised row and which constant includes the coercivity factor. [Sources: `RowValues`, the row-normalisation declarations, `Instance.IsInstanceEntry`, `PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry`; (B.10)–(B.11).]

lean.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry

ties.from: The adjoint reduction replaces difficult pairings by norms of potentials and controlled remainders. The paper gives the analytic consequences in (B.51) but does not specify the full potential coefficient format. `PotentialSeries` and its validity predicate supply one explicit sufficient representation. The meanings of the flux indices, the pressure correction and weak derivatives matter when reading (B.52). A sign or transpose should be compared after reconstructing the operator it represents. ties.from: **A zero scale has defined semantics.** A positive-order node coefficient is multiplied by a power of the inverse scale. At scale zero that factor is zero in Lean; the order-zero factor remains one. A checker can reproduce the totalised map, or justify stronger nonzero-scale assumptions before using an invertible change of basis. These are different implementation choices. Rejecting zero scales is not a newly discovered theorem hypothesis. [Source: `ScaledJetAxis.convert`, lines 4140–4147; `HasSymmetricScale`, line 4151; round-three guard G7.]

ties.from: **Merge repeated channels before using orthogonality.** `AzimuthalBounded` requires injective triples of component, temporal frequency and azimuthal order. Two identical amplitudes in one channel combine before squaring. For angular order \(n_p\), the bound uses \((|n_p|+1/2)^{-2}\); the circular components \(R_1+iR_2,R_1-iR_2,R_3\) have weights \(1/2,1/2,1\), and time has period one. Keeping duplicate rows in a sum of squares can undercount the norm. [Source: lines 3576–3585; p.66 and (B.50).]
